reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5, curriculum and design work delegated by George
factChecks: Independently recomputed every numerical and verdict key in packages/curriculum/tests/philosophy-content.test.ts: 78 lesson questions, 26 recall cards and 39 course-check items. Validity and row counts come from a hand-written truth-table search in the test, posteriors from Bayes' theorem, machine outputs from a hand-run 20p drinks machine, and expected utilities, averages and maximin floors from arithmetic. Each named answer is checked against the text marker, including rejection of the tempting wrong verdict where one exists.

Attributions confirmed in fetched SEP entries on 6 October: Ginet's fake barns published by Goldman (1976), the no-false-lemmas and safety responses, Russell's stopped clock (SEP dates Human Knowledge 1923 although it appeared in 1948, so the course gives no year), Searle 1980 with the systems reply, his memorise-the-rules answer and 'syntax is not sufficient for semantics', Aquinas as origin of double effect, Foot 1967 and Thomson 1985, Putnam 1967 on multiple realisation, Dretske and Nozick rejecting closure, Moore 1939, Place's early identity theory and Harsanyi's average-utility objection to maximin. Not re-fetched and resting on the author's knowledge of the primary literature: Gettier's coins case, Elisabeth's 1643 letter, Reid's brave officer, Parfit's fission and branch-line cases, Thomson's loop, Scanlon's transmitter room and the 20p drinks machine, which adapts Block's Coke-machine example to pence.

Primary-text claims were checked in the Project Gutenberg files themselves: the Milo passage in Nicomachean Ethics II.6 (eBook 8438), 'solitary, poore, nasty, brutish, and short' in Leviathan (3207), Kant's false promise and 'never as means only' (5682), 'better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied' (11224) and chapter XXVII 'Of Identity and Diversity' in Locke's Essay volume 1 (10615, based on the second edition).

Licences verified on 6 October 2026: the OpenStax Introduction to Philosophy preface states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (not CC BY as first assumed), so all ten OpenStax sections are recorded as reference only; forall x: Calgary is CC BY 4.0; SEP entries are reference only under the SEP's copyright page; the Gutenberg editions are public domain in the United States. All Discere prose, problems, models and drawings are original.

Walked all 52 beats of the thirteen lessons and all thirteen placement items in a disposable dev stack (mock tutor, throwaway database); every authored answer was marked correct by the live server. Inspected screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 and repaired padding, overlapping mean-scale labels, SVG line spacing on phones, crowded expected-utility labels, a full-width control strip, empty scene bands and low-contrast truth badges. Verified that the map of a passage, the full truth table, Bayes filtering, levelled utilities, veil averages and identity halos stay hidden until an answer is given. The Playwright spec was written but not run by the author, because its fixed ports are shared with the other course authors.
Editorial review is by the authoring agent under delegated authority. There has been no independent human subject review and no documented learner trial.

acceptedWarnings.reason: The flagged list is Hobbes's verbatim phrase 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'; altering its punctuation would misquote Leviathan.
The prompt quotes Hobbes's phrase verbatim so the learner can identify its author.

changes: Added a thirteen-lesson introduction to philosophy in four modules (arguments, knowledge, mind, ethics and politics) with 78 questions, 26 recall cards and 52 answered visual beats.
Added thirteen-item placement, mixed checkpoint and seven-day delayed transfer checks.

Added nine bounded philosophy model kinds with an interactive explorer: argument maps with a truth-row tester, a Bayes population grid, knowledge cases, machine tables, persistence diagrams, trolley scenes, expected-utility areas, a veil-of-ignorance chooser and Aristotle's mean.
